title: Who Runs Endros?
subtitle: The University, the Committee, and everyone else
summary: On paper the University of Verna governs Endros. In practice its Department of Archaeology answers for the Ruins, the independent Gate Evaluation Committee answers for the Gates, and the settlement itself answers to nobody.
content:
> *"In Endros, everybody is in charge of something, and nobody is in charge of Endros."*
> — said on the docks of Endros

Ask who governs Endros and the official answer is short: **the University of Verna**. A University vessel found the Ruins, University scholars named them and the settlement, and the University's claim has never been formally challenged.

The honest answer is longer. The University's authority is real over the Ruins and almost nowhere else. The Gates belong to a separate body, the **Gate Evaluation Committee**, which the University founded and no longer controls. And the settlement itself, the docks, workshops, housing blocks and floating platforms where everyone actually lives, is not really governed by anyone. It is a place where every power, company and society in the world is pushing its own agenda at once.

This entry sets out who answers for what. For how the Ruins came to be found and named, see [[why-we-call-them-the-valeoran-ruins|Why We Call Them the Valeoran Ruins]]. For the University itself, see [[university-of-verna|The University of Verna]].

> **A newcomer's first question, at the docks**
>
> "Who's in charge here?"
>
> The harbour hand looked up from the cargo net. "Of what?"
>
> "Of... Endros."
>
> "The University, if you ask the University." She hauled on the line. "The Committee, if you want to go through a Gate. Nobody, if you want your crate off this ship before dark." She tied it off. "That one's me. Where's it going?"

## The Ruins: the Department of Archaeology

Anything to do with the **Valeoran Ruins themselves** falls to the University's **Department of Archaeology**: surveying them, studying them, recording what is found on and within them, and deciding what work may be done on their structure. Of all the authorities in Endros, it is the one closest to the official story, a University department doing University work on the thing the University found.

The Department's interests do not always match everyone else's. Work at the Ruins tends to move at the speed of documentation, and the people waiting for an access road to clear do not always share the archaeologists' sense of urgency (see the worksite scene in [[university-of-verna|The University of Verna]]).

> **A notice posted at a worksite near the Ruins**
>
> *DEPARTMENT OF ARCHAEOLOGY, UNIVERSITY OF VERNA*
>
> *Work on, beneath or against any Valeoran structure requires the Department's written approval.*
>
> *Fragments, markings and material of the Ruins are not salvage, ballast or souvenirs.*
>
> *If you are unsure whether something is part of the Ruins, it is.*

## The Gates: the Gate Evaluation Committee

Anything to do with **the Gates** belongs to the [[gate-evaluation-committee|Gate Evaluation Committee]]. The University of Verna founded it, and for a time it was effectively a University committee. It is now a **separate body with members from all the factions**: Vardic, Aurelian, Vesperian, Kharadi, Tianzhao and Vernan.

The Committee evaluates and classifies new Gates, keeps their records, and decides how each may be explored: it clears expeditions, restricts dangerous Gates and imposes quarantines. Its working assumptions, learned at the first four Gates, are set out in [[the-first-four-gates|Four Gates, Four Lessons]]. The oldest of them, that no Core is moved without explicit authorization, is the one nobody argues with.

Almost everything else is argued over, because every faction at the table brings its own instincts about the Gates. That is the point of the arrangement: a decision that survives the whole Committee is one no single power can easily call illegitimate.

> **Minutes of the Gate Evaluation Committee (excerpt)**
>
> *Item two. Application for a return expedition to a restricted Gate.*
>
> *The Aurelian member asked that the crew's manifests and equipment lists be filed in advance. Agreed.*
>
> *The Vesperian member asked that the expedition's findings be published in full. The Vernan member asked that they not be published until reviewed. Discussion. Deferred to item five.*
>
> *The Kharadi member asked who would bear the cost of a second evacuation, should one be needed. No answer was recorded.*
>
> *The Tianzhao member asked whether the Gate's classification was still accurate. Referred to the classification sub-committee.*
>
> *The Vardic member asked when the crew could leave. Cleared, subject to the above.*

## The Settlement: Nobody

Everything else in Endros, the settlement as a place to live and work, is **unmanaged**. There is no council, mayor or governor whose word everyone accepts. The University's nominal authority rarely reaches past the Ruins and its own laboratories, and nobody else has a claim the others would recognise.

What the settlement has instead is agendas, all pressing at once:

- **The Aurelian Empire** offers standards, custody and record-keeping to anyone who will adopt them, and insists it claims no sovereignty (see [[the-aurelian-empire|The Aurelian Empire]]).
- **The Kharad Compact** finances expeditions, insures cargo and argues over salvage claims and who owns what comes back (see [[the-kharad-compact|The Kharad Compact]]).
- **The Vesper Republic** works through its societies and clubs, and wants Gate knowledge open to everyone (see [[the-vesper-republic|The Vesper Republic]]).
- **The Tianzhao Mandate** keeps its own carefully ordered enclave, the Pavilion of Celestial Affairs (see [[the-tianzhao-mandate|The Tianzhao Mandate]]).
- **The Vardic Holds** look after their own workers and their own work (see [[the-vardic-holds|The Vardic Holds]]).
- **Nowhere Expeditions**, the company, brings people in, houses them and keeps them moving, and wants the expeditions to keep running.

The Outpost's docks, workshops, watch and infirmary exist because somebody needed them badly enough to build and run them. The Archive does not record a single authority over any of them. The Outpost Sheet's own aspects put it plainly: *Built Fast, Built to Work*, and *Everyone Came Here for Something*.

## What Is Still Unsettled

The arrangement works, mostly, because each authority keeps to its own ground: the Ruins, the Gates, and everything that is neither. The trouble comes where those grounds meet. A Gate opens among the Ruins. A Gate's Resources become the settlement's trade. A quarantine closes a dock.

And one question has no owner at all: **who owns what crews bring back from beyond a Gate?** The Committee decides whether a Core may be moved, not whose it is afterwards. Kharadi jurists have been arguing the point for years (see [[covenant-of-the-one|The Covenant of the One]]), and so has everyone else.
